Consider the following reaction sequence:

Toluene $\xrightarrow{\text{Conc. HNO}_3\text{ + Conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4}$ Major Product (A)

(A) $\xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2\text{/Fe}}$ (B)

(B) $\xrightarrow{\text{1. Sn/HCl; 2. NaNO}_2\text{/HCl (0-5}^\circ\text{C); 3. H}_3\text{PO}_2\text{/H}_2\text{O}}$ (C)

(C) $\xrightarrow{\text{KMnO}_4\text{, H}^+\text{, }\Delta}$ (D)

The structure of the final product (D) is:
questions.solution:
The reaction sequence proceeds as follows:

1. Nitration: Toluene undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution with concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ and $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. The methyl group is ortho/para-directing, and due to steric hindrance, the major product (A) is 4-nitrotoluene (p-nitrotoluene).

2. Bromination: 4-nitrotoluene reacts with $\text{Br}_2\text{/Fe}$. The $-\text{CH}_3$ group is activating and ortho/para-directing, while the $-\text{NO}_2$ group is deactivating and meta-directing. Both direct the incoming bromine electrophile to the position ortho to the methyl group, yielding 2-bromo-4-nitrotoluene (B).

3. Reductive Deamination: Compound (B) is first reduced by $\text{Sn/HCl}$ to 2-bromo-4-methylaniline, which is then diazotized with $\text{NaNO}_2\text{/HCl}$ at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$. Treatment of the diazonium salt with hypophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$) and water replaces the diazonium group with a hydrogen atom. This removes the substituent at position 4, yielding 1-bromo-2-methylbenzene (o-bromotoluene) as product (C).

4. Side-chain Oxidation: Oxidation of (C) with acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ converts the methyl side chain into a carboxylic acid group. The final product (D) is 2-bromobenzoic acid.

Answer: 2-bromobenzoic acid

questions.solution:
The given starting material is propanenitrile ($CH_3CH_2CN$).

Step 1: Partial hydrolysis of propanenitrile using $H_2O_2$ in an alkaline medium ($OH^-$) yields propanamide (A).

Step 4: Reduction of ethyl isocyanide with $LiAlH_4$ yields a secondary amine, N-methylethanamine (D).
$CH_3CH_2NC \xrightarrow{LiAlH_4} CH_3CH_2NHCH_3$ (D)

Thus, the IUPAC name of the final product D is N-methylethanamine.

Answer: N-Methylethanamine

This is only possible if the methyl group is at the meta position with respect to the $-\mathrm{OH}$ group. Thus, 'C' is 3-methylphenol (m-cresol).

Working backwards, 'B' is 3-methylaniline (m-toluidine) and 'A' is 3-methylbenzamide.

questions.question: Which of the following reaction sequences is most suitable for the synthesis of 3,5-dibromotoluene from $p$-toluidine?
questions.solution:
To synthesize 3,5-dibromotoluene from $p$-toluidine (4-methylaniline), we need to introduce two bromine atoms meta to the methyl group. Direct bromination of toluene would yield ortho and para products, so the directing effect of the $-\text{NH}_2$ group must be utilized before it is removed.

Step (i): Reaction of $p$-toluidine with bromine water ($\text{Br}_2(\text{aq})$) leads to polybromination because the $-\text{NH}_2$ group is highly activating. Bromine atoms are added to both available ortho positions relative to the $-\text{NH}_2$ group, yielding 2,6-dibromo-4-methylaniline.

Step (ii): Diazotization with $\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ at $0^\circ\text{C}$ converts the $-\text{NH}_2$ group into a diazonium group ($-\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-$).

Step (iii): Treatment with $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ reduces the diazonium salt, replacing the diazonium group with a hydrogen atom (deamination).

Removing the amino group from 2,6-dibromo-4-methylaniline leaves the two bromine atoms at positions 3 and 5 relative to the methyl group, resulting in the desired product, 3,5-dibromotoluene.

Analyzing the incorrect options:
Option 1 protects the amine, leading to monobromination and ultimately forming 3-bromotoluene.
Option 2 deaminates first to form toluene, which upon bromination gives a mixture of $o$- and $p$-bromotoluene.
Option 4 uses a Sandmeyer reaction ($\text{CuBr}$) instead of deamination, replacing the diazonium group with a third bromine atom to yield 3,4,5-tribromotoluene.

Answer: (i) $\text{Br}_2(\text{aq})$
(ii) $\text{NaNO}_2, \text{HCl}, 0^\circ\text{C}$
(iii) $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2, \text{H}_2\text{O}$

The major final organic product formed is:
questions.solution:
In $p$-nitrotoluene, the $-\text{CH}_3$ group is activating and ortho/para-directing, while the $-\text{NO}_2$ group is deactivating and meta-directing. Finally, vigorous oxidation with acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ under heating oxidizes the alkyl side chain ($-\text{CH}_3$) to a carboxylic acid group ($-\text{COOH}$). The bromine atom on the ring remains unaffected.

The final product is 2-bromobenzoic acid.

questions.question:

Complete acidic hydrolysis of $D$ yields an aromatic carboxylic acid $E$ which has a molar mass of $122 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

The molar mass of the starting amide $A$ is _______ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
The aromatic carboxylic acid $E$ has a molar mass of $122 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$. This corresponds to benzoic acid, $\mathrm{C_6H_5COOH}$ ($72 + 5 + 12 + 32 + 1 = 122 \text{ g mol}^{-1}$).

Tracing the reaction sequence backwards:
Complete acidic hydrolysis of a nitrile ($D$) yields a carboxylic acid. Thus, $D$ is benzonitrile, $\mathrm{C_6H_5CN}$.
Reaction of a diazonium salt ($C$) with $\mathrm{CuCN/KCN}$ yields a nitrile. Thus, $C$ is benzenediazonium chloride, $\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^+Cl^-}$.
Diazotization of a primary aromatic amine ($B$) yields a diazonium salt. Thus, $B$ is aniline, $\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}$.
Hoffmann bromamide degradation of a primary amide ($A$) yields an amine with one less carbon atom. Thus, $A$ is benzamide, $\mathrm{C_6H_5CONH_2}$.

The molecular formula of benzamide is $\mathrm{C_7H_7NO}$.

Answer: $121$

$o$-anisidine (2-methoxyaniline) has two activating groups: $-\text{NH}_2$ and $-\text{OCH}_3$. The $-\text{NH}_2$ group is much more strongly activating and controls the orientation of electrophilic aromatic substitution.

Let $x$ be the number of these isomers that form a diazonium salt which, upon treatment with $\mathrm{H_3PO_2}/\mathrm{H_2O}$, yields toluene.
Let $y$ be the number of these isomers that give a foul-smelling compound when heated with chloroform and ethanolic $\mathrm{KOH}$.

The value of $(x \times y)$ is ________.
questions.question:
Consider all the benzenoid structural isomers of the molecular formula $\mathrm{C_7H_9N}$.
Let $x$ be the number of these isomers that form a diazonium salt which, upon treatment with $\mathrm{H_3PO_2}/\mathrm{H_2O}$, yields toluene.
Let $y$ be the number of these isomers that give a foul-smelling compound when heated with chloroform and ethanolic $\mathrm{KOH}$.

The value of $(x \times y)$ is ________.
questions.solution:
The benzenoid structural isomers of molecular formula $\mathrm{C_7H_9N}$ are:
1. $o$-toluidine (primary aromatic amine)
2. $m$-toluidine (primary aromatic amine)
3. $p$-toluidine (primary aromatic amine)
4. Benzylamine (primary aliphatic amine)
5. $N$-methylaniline (secondary aromatic amine)

Condition for $x$: The isomer must form a stable diazonium salt that undergoes reductive deamination with $\mathrm{H_3PO_2}$ to yield toluene. Only primary aromatic amines undergo this reaction cleanly. The three toluidines ($o$-, $m$-, and $p$-) will form diazonium salts that give toluene upon reduction. Benzylamine forms an unstable diazonium salt that yields benzyl alcohol, and $N$-methylaniline forms an $N$-nitroso compound. Thus, $x = 3$.

Condition for $y$: The carbylamine test (reaction with $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ and ethanolic $\mathrm{KOH}$ to form a foul-smelling isocyanide) is given by all primary amines, both aliphatic and aromatic. Therefore, the three toluidines and benzylamine will give a positive test. $N$-methylaniline, being a secondary amine, will not. Thus, $y = 4$.

The value of $(x \times y) = 3 \times 4 = 12$.

Answer: $12$

Direct nitration of aniline with conc. $\text{HNO}_3$ and conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at $288\text{ K}$ yields three products: A ($51\%$), B ($47\%$), and C ($2\%$).

In a separate experiment, aniline is treated with acetic anhydride in the presence of pyridine, followed by nitration with conc. $\text{HNO}_3$ and conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, and finally subjected to acidic hydrolysis to yield D as the major product.

questions.question:
Direct nitration of aniline with conc. $\text{HNO}_3$ and conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at $288\text{ K}$ yields three products: A ($51\%$), B ($47\%$), and C ($2\%$).

In a separate experiment, aniline is treated with acetic anhydride in the presence of pyridine, followed by nitration with conc. $\text{HNO}_3$ and conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, and finally subjected to acidic hydrolysis to yield D as the major product.

Identify the products B and D respectively.
questions.solution:
In the direct nitration of aniline using a strongly acidic mixture of conc. $\text{HNO}_3$ and conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, a significant portion of aniline is protonated to form the anilinium ion. The $-\text{NH}_3^+$ group is strongly deactivating and meta-directing. As a result, along with the expected para derivative ($51\%$, product A), a large amount of the meta derivative ($47\%$, product B) is formed, with a minor amount of the ortho derivative ($2\%$, product C). Thus, B is $m$-nitroaniline.

To obtain the para isomer almost exclusively, the $-\text{NH}_2$ group is protected by acetylation with acetic anhydride to form acetanilide. The acetyl group decreases the electron density on the nitrogen atom, preventing its protonation in the acidic medium and reducing its activating effect, while remaining ortho/para directing. Nitration of acetanilide yields $p$-nitroacetanilide as the major product due to steric hindrance at the ortho position. Subsequent acidic hydrolysis removes the acetyl group, giving $p$-nitroaniline as the major product D.

Answer: B = $m$-nitroaniline, D = $p$-nitroaniline

In the basic medium, the newly formed amine nitrogen acts as a nucleophile and attacks the carbon bearing the bromine atom via an intramolecular $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ mechanism.

This displaces the bromide ion and closes the ring. Tracking the atoms, the nitrogen connects the benzylic carbon to the ethyl chain, forming a 6-membered nitrogen-containing ring fused to the benzene ring.

The resulting major product is 1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline.

Answer: 1,2,3,4-tetrahydroisoquinoline

questions.solution:
The formation of a substituted $1H$-benzotriazole from a diamine involves the diazotization of a primary amine followed by intramolecular nucleophilic attack by an adjacent secondary amine.

In the product 1,5-dimethyl-$1H$-benzotriazole, the N1 atom bears a methyl group, indicating it originated from a secondary amine ($\text{-NHCH}_3$). The N3 atom originated from the primary amine ($\text{-NH}_2$) which was diazotized.

Mapping the benzotriazole numbering back to the benzene ring:
N1 is attached to the bridgehead carbon C7a.
N3 is attached to the bridgehead carbon C3a.
Thus, C7a corresponds to the carbon bearing the $\text{-NHCH}_3$ group (let's call it C1 of the reactant), and C3a corresponds to the carbon bearing the $\text{-NH}_2$ group (C2 of the reactant).

The numbering of the benzene ring in benzotriazole proceeds from C3a to C4, C5, C6, and C7.
Therefore, C4 of benzotriazole corresponds to C3 of the reactant, and C5 of benzotriazole corresponds to C4 of the reactant.

Since the product has a methyl group at C5, the starting diamine must have a methyl group at C4.
This means the starting material has an $\text{-NHCH}_3$ group at C1, an $\text{-NH}_2$ group at C2, and a $\text{-CH}_3$ group at C4.
The correct IUPAC name for this compound is 4-methyl-$N^1$-methylbenzene-1,2-diamine.

Answer: 4-Methyl-$N^1$-methylbenzene-1,2-diamine

questions.solution:
In the first step, diphenyl ether undergoes nitration. The phenoxy group ($-\text{OPh}$) is an activating and ortho/para-directing group. Due to steric hindrance, the major product P is 4-nitrodiphenyl ether.

In the second step, P is subjected to bromination. The molecule contains two benzene rings: Ring A has a strongly deactivating $-\text{NO}_2$ group, while Ring B is attached to the oxygen atom and does not have a strongly deactivating group. Thus, Ring B is significantly more electron-rich and activated towards electrophilic aromatic substitution than Ring A.

Bromination will selectively occur on the activated Ring B. The directing group for Ring B is the 4-nitrophenoxy group, which is ortho/para-directing. Since 2 equivalents of $\text{Br}_2$ are used, dibromination will take place on Ring B at the available para and one ortho position (or both ortho positions, though para is preferred first). This yields 2,4-dibromophenyl 4-nitrophenyl ether as the major product Q.

Analyzing the hydrogen atoms in Q:
Ring A (containing the $-\text{NO}_2$ group) is 1,4-disubstituted, leaving hydrogen atoms at positions 2, 3, 5, and 6. So, $x = 4$.
Ring B (the other ring, which is brominated) is 1,2,4-trisubstituted, leaving hydrogen atoms at positions 3, 5, and 6. So, $y = 3$.

Therefore, the value of $x \times y = 4 \times 3 = 12$.

Answer: $12$

Benzamide $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) Br}_2 / \text{NaOH}}$ P $\xrightarrow{\text{(ii) NaNO}_2 / \text{HCl, } 0-5^\circ\text{C}}$ Q $\xrightarrow{\text{(iii) H}_3\text{PO}_2, \text{H}_2\text{O}}$ R $\xrightarrow{\text{(iv) CH}_3\text{Cl, anhydrous AlCl}_3}$ S

The final major product (S) is:
questions.solution:
Step (i): Benzamide undergoes Hoffmann bromamide degradation with $\text{Br}_2$ and $\text{NaOH}$ to form aniline (P).
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CONH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2 / \text{NaOH}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$

Step (ii): Aniline reacts with $\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$ to form benzenediazonium chloride (Q).
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2 / \text{HCl}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-$

Step (iii): Benzenediazonium chloride is reduced by hypophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$) in the presence of water to form benzene (R).

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 \xrightarrow{\text{CH}_3\text{Cl, AlCl}_3} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_3$

The final major product (S) is toluene.

questions.question:
Consider the following list of amines:
Ethylamine, Aniline, Benzylamine, tert-Butylamine, N-Methylaniline, p-Toluidine.

How many of the above amines can be successfully prepared using the Gabriel phthalimide synthesis?
questions.solution:
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis involves the nucleophilic substitution ($S_{N}2$) of an alkyl halide by the phthalimide anion, followed by hydrolysis. It is strictly limited to the preparation of unhindered primary aliphatic or aralkyl amines.

1. Ethylamine: It is a primary aliphatic amine. Its corresponding halide (ethyl halide) easily undergoes $S_{N}2$. It can be prepared.
2. Aniline: It is an aromatic amine. Aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion. It cannot be prepared.
3. Benzylamine: It is a primary aralkyl amine. Benzyl halides undergo $S_{N}2$ easily. It can be prepared.
4. tert-Butylamine: Although it is a primary amine, the corresponding tertiary alkyl halide will undergo elimination rather than substitution due to steric hindrance. It cannot be prepared.
5. N-Methylaniline: It is a secondary amine. Gabriel synthesis only yields primary amines. It cannot be prepared.
6. p-Toluidine: It is an aromatic amine. It cannot be prepared.

Thus, only 2 amines (Ethylamine and Benzylamine) can be prepared by this method.

Answer: $2$

Reductive ozonolysis of $\text{B}$ yields formaldehyde and a branched-chain aliphatic aldehyde. The structure of amine $\text{A}$ is:
questions.question: An optically active amine $\text{A}$ ($\text{C}_5\text{H}_{13}\text{N}$) gives a foul-smelling gas when heated with chloroform and alcoholic $\text{KOH}$. Compound $\text{A}$ undergoes exhaustive methylation followed by heating with moist $\text{Ag}_2\text{O}$ to yield an alkene $\text{B}$ as the major product. Reductive ozonolysis of $\text{B}$ yields formaldehyde and a branched-chain aliphatic aldehyde. The structure of amine $\text{A}$ is:
questions.solution:
The positive carbylamine test (foul smell with $\text{CHCl}_3$ and alcoholic $\text{KOH}$) indicates that $\text{A}$ is a primary amine.

Compound $\text{A}$ is optically active, meaning it must contain a chiral carbon atom.

Exhaustive methylation followed by heating with moist $\text{Ag}_2\text{O}$ (Hofmann elimination) yields the least substituted alkene as the major product (Hofmann rule).

Reductive ozonolysis of $\text{B}$ yields formaldehyde ($\text{HCHO}$), which confirms that $\text{B}$ is a terminal alkene (contains a $=\text{CH}_2$ group). The other product is a branched-chain aliphatic aldehyde.

Let us evaluate the options:
First structure: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)\text{CH}_3$ (pentan-2-amine) is a chiral primary amine. Hofmann elimination gives pent-1-ene. Ozonolysis yields formaldehyde and butanal (a straight-chain aldehyde).
Second structure: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ (2-methylbutan-1-amine) is a chiral primary amine. Hofmann elimination gives 2-methylbut-1-ene. Ozonolysis yields formaldehyde and butan-2-one (a ketone).
Third structure: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$ (3-methylbutan-1-amine) is a primary amine but achiral.
Fourth structure: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)\text{CH}_3$ (3-methylbutan-2-amine) is a chiral primary amine. Hofmann elimination occurs preferentially at the less hindered terminal methyl group, giving 3-methylbut-1-ene ($\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$) as the major product. Ozonolysis of this alkene yields formaldehyde and 2-methylpropanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CHO}$), which is a branched-chain aliphatic aldehyde.

Thus, the correct structure is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)\text{CH}_3$.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}(\text{NH}_2)\text{CH}_3$

questions.question:
An organic compound $o$-toluidine is subjected to the following sequence of reactions:
(i) $\text{Br}_2 (aq)$
(ii) $\text{NaNO}_2 / \text{HCl}$, $273-278\text{ K}$
(iii) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, heat

The major final product formed is:
questions.solution:
$o$-toluidine (2-methylaniline) has a strongly activating $-\text{NH}_2$ group which directs the incoming electrophiles to the ortho and para positions.

Step (i): Reaction with aqueous bromine ($\text{Br}_2/\text{H}_2\text{O}$) leads to polyhalogenation. Since one ortho position is occupied by the methyl group, bromination occurs at the remaining ortho (position 6) and para (position 4) positions, yielding 4,6-dibromo-2-methylaniline.

Step (ii): Treatment with $\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}$ at $273-278\text{ K}$ diazotizes the primary amine, forming 4,6-dibromo-2-methylbenzenediazonium chloride.

Step (iii): Heating with ethanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) reduces the diazonium group to a hydrogen atom (deamination), while ethanol itself is oxidized to acetaldehyde.

The $-\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-$ group is replaced by $-\text{H}$. The resulting compound has a methyl group with two bromine atoms at positions 3 and 5 relative to it. Thus, the major final product is 3,5-dibromotoluene.

Answer: 3,5-dibromotoluene

Thus, the final product S is 2-acetoxybenzoic acid.

Aniline with $\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}$ at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$, followed by reaction with $\beta$-naphthol in alkaline medium
Aniline with $\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}$ at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$, followed by reaction with $\alpha$-naphthol in alkaline medium

questions.solution:

In retrosynthetic analysis of azo dyes, the bond is cleaved at the azo group. The aromatic ring with the activating group ($-OH$) acts as the coupling component, while the other ring originates from the diazonium salt.

Here, the coupling component is $\alpha$-naphthol (1-naphthol), which undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution at the para position (C-4) due to the strong activating effect of the $-OH$ group.

The diazonium component is benzenediazonium chloride, which is prepared by the diazotization of aniline using $\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$.

Thus, the correct starting materials are aniline and $\alpha$-naphthol.

Answer: Aniline with $\text{NaNO}_2/\text{HCl}$ at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$, followed by reaction with $\alpha$-naphthol in alkaline medium

An aromatic amide $A$ with the molecular formula $C_{7}H_{7}NO$ is treated with $Br_{2}$ and aqueous $NaOH$ to give compound $B$. Compound $B$ is then reacted with Hinsberg's reagent to form compound $C$, which is found to be soluble in aqueous $NaOH$.

Determine the number of carbon atoms present in one molecule of compound $C$.
questions.question:
An aromatic amide $A$ with the molecular formula $C_{7}H_{7}NO$ is treated with $Br_{2}$ and aqueous $NaOH$ to give compound $B$. Compound $B$ is then reacted with Hinsberg's reagent to form compound $C$, which is found to be soluble in aqueous $NaOH$.

Determine the number of carbon atoms present in one molecule of compound $C$.
questions.solution:
The aromatic amide $A$ with molecular formula $C_{7}H_{7}NO$ is benzamide ($C_{6}H_{5}CONH_{2}$).

Treatment of benzamide with $Br_{2}$ and aqueous $NaOH$ brings about the Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction. In this reaction, the carbonyl carbon is lost as carbonate, yielding aniline ($C_{6}H_{5}NH_{2}$) as compound $B$.

Aniline is a primary amine. It reacts with Hinsberg's reagent, which is benzenesulfonyl chloride ($C_{6}H_{5}SO_{2}Cl$), to form N-phenylbenzenesulfonamide as compound $C$.
The reaction is:
$C_{6}H_{5}NH_{2} + C_{6}H_{5}SO_{2}Cl \rightarrow C_{6}H_{5}-NH-SO_{2}-C_{6}H_{5} + HCl$

Compound $C$ has an acidic hydrogen attached to nitrogen, making it soluble in aqueous $NaOH$.
The structure of $C$ is $C_{6}H_{5}-NH-SO_{2}-C_{6}H_{5}$.
The number of carbon atoms in compound $C$ is $6$ (from the aniline ring) $+ 6$ (from the benzenesulfonyl ring) $= 12$.

Answer: $12$

Identify the starting isomer of nitrotoluene.
questions.question:
An isomer of nitrotoluene undergoes the following sequence of reactions to yield 4-chlorobenzoic acid as the final major product:
1. $\text{Cl}_2 / \text{FeCl}_3$
2. $\text{Fe} / \text{HCl}$
3. $\text{NaNO}_2 / \text{HCl}, 0-5^\circ\text{C}$
4. $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2 / \text{H}_2\text{O}$
5. Alk. $\text{KMnO}_4, \Delta$ followed by $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$

Identify the starting isomer of nitrotoluene.
questions.solution:
Working backwards from the final product:

The final product is 4-chlorobenzoic acid. Step 5 (oxidation with alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$) oxidizes an alkyl side chain to a $-\text{COOH}$ group. Thus, the precursor before oxidation must be 4-chlorotoluene.

The total number of $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized carbon atoms in the major product (C) is ________.
questions.question:
Consider the following sequence of reactions:

p-toluidine $\xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2, \text{ HCl, } 0-5^\circ\text{C}}$ (A) $\xrightarrow{\text{phenol, NaOH}}$ (B) $\xrightarrow{\text{(i) CHCl}_3\text{, NaOH, } \Delta \text{ (ii) H}_3\text{O}^+}$ (C)

The total number of $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized carbon atoms in the major product (C) is ________.
questions.solution:
Step 1: p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) reacts with $\text{NaNO}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$ at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$ to form p-toluenediazonium chloride (A).

Step 2: The diazonium salt (A) couples with phenol in a basic medium. The coupling takes place at the para position of phenol, producing 4-(4-methylphenylazo)phenol (B).

Step 3: Compound (B) is subjected to the Reimer-Tiemann reaction conditions ($\text{CHCl}_3$ and $\text{NaOH}$, followed by acidic workup). The phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group strongly activates the ring towards electrophilic aromatic substitution. Since the para position is already occupied by the azo group, formylation occurs at the ortho position. The major product (C) is 2-hydroxy-5-(4-methylphenylazo)benzaldehyde.

The structure of (C) contains:
- One p-tolyl ring, which has 6 $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized carbons and 1 $\text{sp}^3$ hybridized carbon (the methyl group).
- One phenolic ring, which has 6 $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized carbons.
- One aldehyde group ($-\text{CHO}$), which has 1 $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized carbon.

Total number of $\text{sp}^2$ hybridized carbon atoms = $6 + 6 + 1 = 13$.

Answer: $13$

questions.q: When benzenediazonium chloride is treated with $p$-cresol in an alkaline medium, the major product formed is:
questions.question: When benzenediazonium chloride is treated with $p$-cresol in an alkaline medium, the major product formed is:
questions.solution:
Azo coupling is an electrophilic aromatic substitution where the diazonium ion acts as a weak electrophile. It requires a highly activated aromatic ring to react.

In $p$-cresol (4-methylphenol), there are two substituents on the benzene ring: an $-\text{OH}$ group and a $-\text{CH}_3$ group. Both are activating and ortho/para directing, but the $-\text{OH}$ group is a much stronger activating group than the $-\text{CH}_3$ group. Therefore, the $-\text{OH}$ group dictates the regiochemistry of the incoming electrophile.

The position para to the $-\text{OH}$ group is already blocked by the $-\text{CH}_3$ group. As a result, the electrophilic attack by the benzenediazonium ion must occur at the position ortho to the $-\text{OH}$ group.

This leads to the formation of 2-hydroxy-5-methylazobenzene as the major product.

Answer: 2-hydroxy-5-methylazobenzene
